rulingGate.verdict: PASS (no real production flow loses an effect under the flip). (1) r1, r2, r3 (command route) and c1 (co-op HirePilot door) keep their effect in the journal projection after the whole-campaign save under the flip, and the saved record carries balance and day (pilots are not represented by the record and survive in the journal). (2) Combat outcome through appendCombatOutcomeBatch: the outcome now rewrites the saved record on first commit (version 1 -> 2, roster readiness Destroyed/Damaged, unit-0 kept, not removed); o1c, o2 and o2u survive the probe's host save; o1 and o1s are RED under the flip exactly as the re-admission describes them, because their host save is accepted at the version the outcome's rewrite produced while carrying a Ready/Ready roster. From the code, no production client can make that save (realFlows.combatOutcome): every co-op whole-campaign PUT is the persistence store's putLiveCampaign at its held baseVersion, and every path that sets baseVersion to a server-written version restores the roster store from that same record's rosterProjection. Measured through the real client stores (rows h1-h3, fetch wired to the live route): a host holding the pre-outcome version is refused 409, rolled back to the server record (roster store Destroyed/Damaged), and its next save keeps the outcome in the journal and the record, on the baseline and under the flip; U35g's committed rows suite (host save at the held version, 409, then the server record) is 8/8 under the flip. (3) RosterUnitChanged: survives in every real flow above. Salvage recovery (recoveredUnit, row s1): lost from the journal by the host's save on both sides once journal-native (scoped out by the owner, FN-u35d-recovered-unit-lost; no production producer).

risksForTheParent: Authority (the owner's ruling on the head): once merged, every campaign the PUT route creates is journal-native (genesis, journal-native marker, effective branch), every whole-campaign save of it is a checkpoint, the adopt route writes journal-native markers, and co-op host creation runs the checkpoint's genesis-branch step.

Authority/concurrency: a first-receipt combat outcome now moves the saved record's version on every new co-op campaign, so a host save built before it is refused 409 with a toast and the host's local change (for example Return to Campaign's mission completion and unitCombatStates carry-forward, which precede the save) is rolled back to the server record (measured in h1/h3: roster store Destroyed/Damaged after the rollback); the outcome itself survives. This was already true for journal-native campaigns since U35g; the flip makes it the default for new campaigns.
Idempotency: unchanged by the flip; the outcome inbox rewrites only on the first receipt (U35g row i passes under the flip).

Migration: after the flip, co-op creation of a campaign created before the flip fails at the genesis-branch step (campaignCreationCheckpoint requires the journal-native marker; the unit/api row pins the 500); under OD-mvp-hard-cutover no pre-cutover data is protected, but a local dev database will show it.

The two two-process specs are re-pinned from an in-process measurement, not run: they cannot start in a junctioned worktree; the main proof in the root checkout must run both, --workers=1 (FN-u22-two-process-specs-share-port-3617).
Owner ruling: authority, idempotency and migration review classes need the head-bound Lane B ruling on the head that merges.
